insights.headline: Fed-hike bets fade as MCX gold climbs past Rs 1.48 lakh; oil slide adds support
insights.summary: MCX December gold rose to Rs 1,48,379 per 10 grams and silver to Rs 2,12,013 per kg as Fed Chair Warsh's Bangkok remarks cut October hike odds below 20%, though a firmer rupee capped domestic gains. Spot gold held near $4,185 with silver at $57.80, and falling oil prices added support with New York futures up 0.5% to $4,203. A December Fed hike is still priced at nearly 89% ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.
points: MCX Dec gold Rs 1,48,379/10g (+Rs 461); Dec silver Rs 2,12,013/kg (+Rs 826) as October Fed hike bets faded.
Spot gold ~$4,185, silver ~$57.80; NY gold futures +0.5% to $4,203 as oil prices fell.
RBI set SGB 2020-21 Series VII premature redemption at Rs 14,614 for Oct 19 - about 192% gains.
IBJA's Surendra Mehta sees gold rallying 10-12% to $4,700/oz by November 30.
Silver stalls below $58; FXEmpire flags $58.65 as the pivot for a counter-trend rally.

trending.title: Warsh cools October hike bets; metals rebound
trending.summary: Warsh's Bangkok remarks unwound October hike bets to under 20%, lifting spot gold toward $4,200 and silver to $57.80. A December hike (~89% odds) is still in play; the Oct 27-28 FOMC meet is next.

trending.title: Oil's slide joins the bullion tailwinds
trending.summary: Falling crude eased inflation fears and lifted gold, with NY futures up 0.5% to $4,203. US-Iran tensions and West Asia worries keep the backdrop volatile into a Dussehra-shortened week.

trending.title: Silver's $58 ceiling in focus
trending.summary: Silver stalls below $58 despite dollar weakness; FXEmpire flags $58.65 as the pivot - a break opens $61.74-$62.45, failure risks a $55.56 retest. On MCX, silver outpaced gold's rebound.

trending.title: Dhanteras playbook: ritual yes, rethink the investment
trending.summary: Mint's Dhanteras piece separates festive ritual from investment logic, as RBI's Rs 14,614 SGB redemption price hands Series VII holders ~192% gains. Jewellery demand meets a week of choppy prices.

items.title: Gold, silver trade higher as Fed rate hike concerns ease
items.summary: MCX December gold traded at Rs 1,48,379/10g (+0.31%) and silver at Rs 2,12,013/kg (+0.39%) Monday morning, tracking firm global cues. Per IANS, Fed Chair Warsh's Bangkok remarks cut the implied October hike chance below 20%; hot PPI keeps a December move in play ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meet. COMEX gold neared $4,200 (+0.5%), silver $57.80 (+0.89%), but a firmer rupee capped domestic gains.

items.title: Gold edges higher as traders ease rate-hike bets on Warsh speech
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.5% to $4,184.55 an ounce and silver 1.5% to $57.82 in Singapore, as Fed Chair Warsh's remarks unwound October hike bets to less than one-in-six. A hot US inflation print had fuelled hike expectations, but Warsh halted the dollar's advance. Gold has held above $4,000 since August with 13 straight weeks of ETF inflows; traders still see a high chance of a hike before year-end.

items.title: Gold Rises Amid Falling Oil Prices
items.summary: Gold rose in early European trade as falling oil prices eased inflation worries, with New York futures up 0.5% to $4,203.30 an ounce. Saxo Bank analysts described a tug of war between macro sellers and safe-haven buyers amid geopolitical and fiscal tensions. Traders see only a 15% chance of an October Fed hike but nearly 89% for December.

items.title: Gold and silver head for volatile week amid crude oil spike, West Asia worries
items.summary: PTI reports MCX December gold fell Rs 3,581 (-2.4%) last week to Rs 1.47 lakh/10g, and silver Rs 14,568 (-6.4%) to Rs 2.11 lakh/kg. The rupee's jump to 94.8 from ~96.8 in five sessions on RBI intervention cut import costs, dragging domestic prices down ~5x the global fall. Analysts expect a capped, choppy week: Brent near $110, West Asia tensions, and Tuesday's Dussehra morning closure.

items.title: Gold and silver prices rise in India amid US-Iran tensions
items.summary: Indian bullion gained in Monday morning trade as US-Iran tensions kept safe-haven demand firm while investors weighed crude prices and the US rate outlook. Reuters-cited data: spot gold up 0.4% to $4,182.30 an ounce, spot silver up 1.3% to $57.73, and US December gold futures up 0.5% to $4,203.50. Traders await US data, energy-price moves and Middle East signals ahead of the Fed's next decision.

items.title: IBJA's Surendra Mehta sees gold rallying 10-12% to $4,700 by November 30
items.summary: IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET Now Swadesh he expects gold to rally 10-12% by November 30, potentially reaching $4,700 an ounce, as bond yields ease below 5.1% and crude stabilises near $105. He put the downside at 4-5% (a move toward $3,850 not ruled out) and said India's festive season could support prices, barring fresh geopolitical escalation.

items.title: China's gold buying reflects push to diversify reserves and household demand
items.summary: The People's Bank of China bought gold for a 23rd straight month in September, adding about 23 tonnes - its biggest monthly purchase in nearly three years - lifting reported holdings to around 2,410 tonnes, or 8.5% of reserves. The accumulation reflects reserve diversification away from US debt after the 2022 Russia asset freeze, alongside Chinese household demand for bars and coins.

items.title: Silver stalls below $58.00 despite US dollar weakness
items.summary: XAG/USD kept a moderately bullish tone but bulls failed to find acceptance near the $58.00 area, with the US dollar index edging down less than 0.1% on Monday. Markets priced only a 12% chance of an October Fed hike, down from nearly 60% a month ago, after Chair Warsh declined forward guidance; elevated energy prices kept inflation well above target.

items.title: Silver (XAG) Forecast: Bounce Builds but Rate Trade Keeps Sellers in Control
items.summary: FXEmpire's technical take: silver is bouncing inside a $61.74-$55.56 range, with the 50% level at $58.65 the key upside pivot - a sustained break above could open $61.74-$62.45, while failure risks a retest of last week's $55.56 low. The bias stays down while silver sits below its 50-day average near $64.41, with yields and the dollar setting the tone.

items.title: Why is gold falling even as ETF investors and central banks pile in?
items.summary: Analysis notes gold fell to $4,093 an ounce on October 14, down 26% from January's $5,595 record, as the September 16 Fed hike pushed 10-year Treasury yields to 24-year highs. Fund managers say ETF investors kept buying while futures traders sold; in their view, the bull market could resume if the Fed or Treasury caps yields, with stubborn inflation forcing more hikes as the main risk.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2020-21 Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614 for October 19
items.summary: The RBI has fixed October 19, 2026 as the premature redemption date for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per gram, based on IBJA's average closing prices of October 14-16. Online subscribers gain 192.22% and offline buyers 189.33% in capital gains, alongside 2.5% annual interest; holders must route requests through their receiving offices within the notification window.

items.title: Gold on Dhanteras: celebrate the ritual, rethink the investment
items.summary: A Mint column argues Dhanteras gold buying is a cherished tradition that should not be mistaken for investing: most purchases are jewellery with making charges that vanish on resale, or coins sitting in rented lockers. Buying an asset on a set date because it is auspicious is consumption, not a financial plan - enjoy the ritual, but judge the purchase on its merits.
